main_body: Two stacked horizontal logs lying on their sides. Round cut ends with growth rings face left/front, and dark bark bodies run to the right.
top_band: No distinct top band. The upper log has only a thin 1-2 row lighter brown highlight along its back/top edge (rows ~3-5), which is a rim and not a horizontal surface.
evidence: Reading a column through the bark of the upper log (x~13-17), I meet a 1-2 row light edge, then dark brown bark down to the bottom. There is no multi-row lighter top surface, no front-edge step and no eave shadow. The cylinders are shown in side profile, and the circular cut ends are vertical faces seen nearly face-on. The log tops that should be visible from above are only a thin rim, so this reads as a side elevation of a log pile and not a 3/4 object.

style.evidence: The cut ends have a few cream-to-tan ring steps and a small amount of detail. The bark bodies are large, nearly flat dark-brown areas with only a faint highlight line and no bark grain or per-log texture. The outline is a very dark brown that leans near-black in places. Overall it is much thinner than the stall and well references, which carry many colours per tile, so it would look flatter next to them.
